svg.title: Cross-tenant Fabric SQL: home MFA, provider authorization, and validation gaps
svg.desc: The proposed BCH guest tenant owns human identity, groups, and applicable Conditional Access policies. An MFA-capable client connects over TDS to an Epic-hosted Fabric SQL endpoint only if Epic is the confirmed provider. Fabric-managed mappings authorize the provider-local identity. A separate provider external-MFA setting needs end-to-end validation. Classic B2B, local passwords or keys, and workload identities are distinct paths.
svg.text: Cross-tenant SQL authorization and MFA: separate the enforcement layers
Fabric special mapping flow - not classic B2B guest-user trust, an AD forest trust, or OneLake shortcut sharing
Proposed roles: BCH = guest/home identity; Epic = provider/resource. Actual tenant ownership and feature use must be confirmed.
BCH home tenant - identity and policy
Native human identity and approved source group
BCH manages membership and home authentication
Group mapping is not proof of literal cross-directory nesting
Applicable Conditional Access and MFA
Identify the actual target resource applications
Require the approved MFA / device controls
Prior MFA claim can satisfy access without a new prompt
SSMS / approved Entra-aware client
Use Microsoft Entra MFA / interactive authentication
Use provider-generated guest-specific SQL endpoint
Entra password-only cannot satisfy required MFA
Epic provider tenant - only if confirmed
Fabric-managed mapping objects
Local service principals / groups represent guest identities
Provider grants permissions; guest owns source membership
Separate provider outside-organization MFA setting
Documented default: off; organization-wide scope
Microsoft must confirm original-human claim handling
App-only behavior and session rechecks need validation
Provider SQL endpoint and data permissions
Item Read permits connection; SQL grants limit data
Pilot: SELECT on approved view, deny unintended access
Home sign-in success is not permission to every table
Entra-authenticated TDS 1433
Original identity plus mapping
Arrows abstract internal token processing
Consent and principal mapping
Not a network tunnel or B2B invite
Evidence gate - combine home authentication, provider authorization, and real allow / deny tests
Home logs: Application versus Resource, policy result, Authentication Details, prior-MFA claim, required device control.
Provider: mapping and grants, external MFA setting, SP sign-ins, Purview events, approved view and denied base-table tests.
A provider service-principal sign-in does not prove original-human MFA. Report-only CA does not establish enforcement.
Generic Fabric CA baseline: Power BI Service, Azure Data Explorer, Azure SQL Database, Azure Storage, Azure Cosmos DB.
Verify actual per-client resource/audience coverage. Do not treat the Warehouse hostname as an automatically separate CA application.
Classic Azure SQL B2B is different
Resource CA can require MFA.
Inbound trust can accept home MFA.
Without trust, resource MFA can be required.
Do not assume this is Fabric's mapping flow.
Passwords, keys, and workloads differ
Fabric does not support native SQL logins.
Cosmos keys do not invoke Entra MFA.
Apps / managed identities have no human prompt.
Cosmos external-user path needs its own validation.
Existing SQL sessions are a separate gate
Consent revoke: within a day, sessions unaffected.
Fabric CAE session control is not supported.
Mapping-delete open-session effect needs testing.
Do not promise immediate session termination.

Prepared October 15, 2026. Research-derived architecture, not deployment certification. No production sign-ins or data queries were performed.
